title.narrative: Marport Liman Isletmeleri Sanayi Ve Ticaret Anonim Sirketi

description.narrative: 1) Stakeholder effects: The Project would increase berth capacity and equipment that enables Marport to serve better to container traffic in Türkiye with more efficient and safer port operations for all vessel types and sizes. 2) Environmental effects: The Project would add energy efficient equipment to Marport operation, which will contribute avoid GHG emissions in Türkiyes carbon-intensive transportation sector. 3) Contribution to market creation -Integration: The Project strengthens connectivity in the Black Sea region by improving transshipment capabilities at a key gateway Port thereby contributing to maintain integration of the Black Sea region to global markets.

The project entails supporting the third largest container terminal in Türkiye - Marport Liman Isletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Marport) by the implementation of an investment plan to (i) refurbish and extend existing berths and procure new equipment; in order to improve productivity and enhance safe servicing of larger vessels and, (ii) refinance an existing bridge loan due in early 2023 (the Project). Marport has been operational since 2001 under an operating permit and maintaining stable profitability and cash flows. IFC's support entails an IFC A loan of US$105.5 million, mobilization of US$94.5 million Managed Co-lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) loan and US$6 million Loan-equivalent (LEQ) exposure for interest rate swaps..

name.narrative: Marport is in Ambarli Port Facility, along with three other adjacent ports, about 20 km from Istanbul on the north shore of the Marmara Sea on the European side of the Bosphorus. Marport handles cargo mainly for Istanbul and Türkiyes European side together with the extended hinterland thereof thanks to variable liners and corridors served, as well as transshipment to other Türkiye ports, the Black Sea region, and some other European countries.
